flashcard_questions.q: What does the law of reflection state?
flashcard_questions.a: The angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the normal in a ray diagram?
flashcard_questions.a: An imaginary line drawn at 90° to the surface where the ray hits.

flashcard_questions.q: How do the particles move in a sound wave?
flashcard_questions.a: Back and forth parallel to the direction the wave travels.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
flashcard_questions.a: It is a mechanical wave, so it needs a medium.

flashcard_questions.q: Through which state of matter does sound travel fastest?
flashcard_questions.a: Solids, because their particles are closest together.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the speed of sound in air at room temperature?
What is the range of normal human hearing?
What are sound waves above 20,000 Hz called?
Which property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
Which property of a sound wave determines its loudness?
Why must you halve the distance in an echo calculation?
flashcard_questions.a: The sound travels to the surface and back again.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is ultrasound preferred to X-rays for scanning a foetus?
flashcard_questions.a: It is non-invasive and does not cause the cell damage ionising radiation can.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of wave are seismic P-waves?
Which type of wave are seismic S-waves?
What does the S-wave shadow zone prove about the Earth's outer core?
flashcard_questions.a: That it is liquid, because S-waves cannot pass through liquids.
